To solve the problem, we are given that a matrix $\mathbf{A}$ satisfies the following two equations:

$$
\mathbf{A} \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{A} \begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ 2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -5 \\ -5 \end{pmatrix}
$$

We are asked to compute:

$$
\mathbf{A} \begin{pmatrix} -13 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}
$$

---

### Step 1: Express the target vector as a linear combination

We aim to express the vector $\begin{pmatrix} -13 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$ as a linear combination of the two known vectors:

$$
\begin{pmatrix} -13 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} = a \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} + b \begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ 2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}
$$

This gives us the system of equations:

$$
\begin{cases}
3a - 5b = -13 \\
a + 2b = 3 \\
2b = 4
\end{cases}
$$

From the third equation, we find:

$$
b = 2
$$

Substitute into the second equation:

$$
a + 2(2) = 3 \Rightarrow a = 3 - 4 = -1
$$

Now verify the first equation:

$$
3(-1) - 5(2) = -3 - 10 = -13 \quad \text{✓}
$$

So, the vector can be expressed as:

$$
\begin{pmatrix} -13 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} = -1 \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} + 2 \begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ 2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}
$$

---

### Step 2: Use linearity of matrix multiplication

By the linearity of matrix multiplication:

$$
\mathbf{A} \begin{pmatrix} -13 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} = -1 \mathbf{A} \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} + 2 \mathbf{A} \begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ 2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}
$$

$$
= -1 \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix} + 2 \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -5 \\ -5 \end{pmatrix}
$$

$$
-1 \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ -4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}
$$
$$
2 \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -5 \\ -5 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -10 \\ -10 \end{pmatrix}
$$

Add the two results:

$$
\begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ -4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -10 \\ -10 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ -14 \\ -7 \end{pmatrix}
$$
